title: Sur la distribution des nombres premiers
extractedQuote: The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log x).
plainSummary: Proves that classical RH is equivalent to square-root error O(sqrt(x) log x) in the Prime Number Theorem.
plainImpactUpgrade: Square-root Prime Number Theorem error O(sqrt(x) log x) holds unconditionally.
plainFallbackNote: De la Vallee Poussin's unconditional zero-free region gives O(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))).

title: Sharper bounds for the Chebyshev functions theta(x) and psi(x). II
extractedQuote: If the Riemann hypothesis is true, then |pi(x) - Li(x)| < sqrt(x) log(x) / (8 pi) for all x >= 2657.
plainSummary: Gives explicit numerical constants for prime-counting error |pi(x) - Li(x)| < sqrt(x) log(x) / (8 pi) for all x >= 2,657 under RH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Explicit constant 1/(8 pi) on sqrt(x) log x prime-counting error becomes unconditional for all x >= 2,657.
plainFallbackNote: Explicit unconditional zero-free-region bounds (Dusart / Mossinghoff-Trudgian) hold with larger error.

title: Grandes valeurs de la fonction somme des diviseurs et hypothese de Riemann
extractedQuote: RH is true if and only if sigma(n) < e^gamma n log log n for every integer n > 5040.
plainSummary: Robin's divisor-sum inequality sigma(n) < e^gamma n log log n for n > 5,040 — equivalent to RH and now machine-checked in Lean 4.
plainImpactUpgrade: Compiled as an unconditional Lean 4 theorem (`robin_inequality`) with zero hypotheses.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional proof of sigma(n) < e^gamma n log log n for all n > 5,040 existed without RH.

title: An Elementary Problem Equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis
extractedQuote: Show, for each n >= 1, that sum_{d|n} d <= H_n + exp(H_n) log(H_n), with equality only for n = 1. Theorem 1.1: Problem E is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis.
quoteLocator: Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002), Theorem 1.1; Sutherland ArithChallenge.lean
plainSummary: Rewrites classical RH as an elementary harmonic-number bound on divisor sums for all n >= 1 — now machine-checked in Lean 4.
plainImpactUpgrade: Compiled as an unconditional Lean 4 theorem (`lagarias_inequality`) with zero hypotheses.
plainFallbackNote: Exact biconditional equivalence with classical RH.

title: On the least prime in an arithmetical progression
extractedQuote: In 1934, Chowla showed GRH for Dirichlet L-functions implies the first prime p = a mod m is O(m^2 (log m)^2).
quoteLocator: J. Indian Math. Soc. 1 (1934); MathOverflow Q17209 (i)
plainSummary: Bounds the smallest prime in an arithmetic progression a mod m by O(m^2 (log m)^2) using Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Covered by Dirichlet GRH: slashes Linnik's unconditional m^5 exponent down to O(m^2 (log m)^2) (explicitly <= (phi(m) log m)^2 via Lamzouri-Li-Soundararajan).
plainFallbackNote: Linnik's theorem (Xylouris 2011) bounds the least prime unconditionally by O(m^5).

title: The Least Quadratic Non Residue
extractedQuote: GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions implies that the first nonmember of every proper subgroup of (Z/mZ)* is O((log m)^2).
plainSummary: Guarantees a quadratic non-residue modulo p of size O((log p)^2) under Dirichlet GRH, making deterministic Tonelli-Shanks square roots fast.
plainImpactUpgrade: Covered by Dirichlet GRH: deterministic search for a quadratic non-residue mod p finishes in O((log p)^2) steps.
plainFallbackNote: Burgess's character-sum bound gives unconditional p^{1/(4 sqrt(e)) + eps}, and randomized Tonelli-Shanks succeeds in expected O(1) trials.

title: Riemann's hypothesis and tests for primality
extractedQuote: In 1976, Gary Miller introduced a deterministic primality test that he could prove runs in polynomial time using GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions.
quoteLocator: J. Comput. System Sci. 13 (1976), 300-317; MathOverflow Q17209 (f)
plainSummary: Proves that deterministic Miller primality testing runs in polynomial time assuming Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Covered by Dirichlet GRH: deterministic Miller primality testing runs in proven O~(log^4 n) time (with Bach's 2(ln n)^2 cutoff).
plainFallbackNote: AKS (2002) already proved PRIMES in P unconditionally in O~(log^6 n), and randomized Miller-Rabin is standard in practice.

title: Explicit bounds for primality testing and related problems
extractedQuote: Bach showed GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions implies each proper subgroup of (Z/mZ)* is missing some integer from 1 to 2(log m)^2.
plainSummary: Pins down the exact constant 2(ln n)^2 on Miller's deterministic primality witness bound under Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Covered by Dirichlet GRH: testing witnesses up to 2(ln n)^2 is unconditionally sufficient to certify primality.
plainFallbackNote: AKS (2002) proves deterministic polynomial-time primality unconditionally with higher exponent.

title: Complete Vinogradov 3-primes theorem under the Riemann hypothesis
authors: J.-M. Deshouillers, G. Effinger, H. te Riele, D. Zinoviev
extractedQuote: In 1997, Deshouillers, Effinger, te Riele, and Zinoviev showed GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions implies the odd Goldbach conjecture for all odd n >= 7. This is an obsolete application since Helfgott proved odd Goldbach unconditionally in 2013.
quoteLocator: Electron. Res. Announc. Amer. Math. Soc. 3 (1997); MathOverflow Q17209 (g)
plainSummary: Proved weak (ternary) Goldbach for all odd n >= 7 under Dirichlet GRH — later proved unconditionally by Helfgott in 2013.
plainImpactUpgrade: Covered by Dirichlet GRH, making this 1997 proof route unconditional alongside Helfgott's 2013 unconditional proof.
plainFallbackNote: Harald Helfgott (2013) already proved the weak Goldbach conjecture unconditionally for every odd n >= 7.

title: Conditional bounds for the least quadratic non-residue and related problems
authors: Youness Lamzouri, Xiannan Li, Kannan Soundararajan
extractedQuote: Lamzouri, Li, and Soundararajan proved that GRH for Dirichlet L-functions implies the least prime p = a mod q is <= (phi(q) log q)^2 and gives explicit class-number lower bounds for Q(sqrt(-d)).
quoteLocator: Math. Comp. 84 (2015), Theorems 1.1-1.4; MathOverflow Q17209 (f, k)
plainSummary: Sharpens Bach's witness bound to (log m)^2 and proves explicit least-prime and imaginary-quadratic class-number bounds under Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Covered by Dirichlet GRH: explicit (phi(q) log q)^2 least-prime bound and (log m)^2 subgroup-witness bound hold unconditionally.
plainFallbackNote: Unconditional Linnik and Burgess bounds hold with much weaker exponents.

title: Prime Twins and Siegel Zeros
extractedQuote: If exceptional Landau-Siegel real zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions exist infinitely often (violating Dirichlet GRH), then the Twin Prime Conjecture holds.
plainSummary: Proved that if Dirichlet GRH failed via infinitely many Siegel zeros, Twin Primes would follow — a conditional route now ruled out.
plainImpactUpgrade: Dirichlet GRH rules out Landau-Siegel zeros, retiring this counterfactual route to Twin Primes as vacuous.
plainFallbackNote: Twin Primes remains open unconditionally (best proven gap bound is <= 246 via Maynard-Tao / Polymath8b).

title: Chebyshev's Bias
extractedQuote: Assuming GRH for Dirichlet L-functions AND the Linear Independence hypothesis (GSH) on positive imaginary parts of zeros, the logarithmic density of x with pi(x; 4, 3) > pi(x; 4, 1) exists and equals 0.9959...
plainSummary: Explains why primes = 3 mod 4 lead primes = 1 mod 4 99.59% of the time — needs BOTH Dirichlet GRH and Grand Simplicity (linear independence of zeros), which stays open!
plainImpactUpgrade: Even with Dirichlet GRH checked, Rubinstein-Sarnak's prime-race density still waits on linear independence of zero ordinates (GSH).
plainFallbackNote: Without GSH (linear independence of zeros), even Dirichlet GRH alone does not settle the exact prime-race logarithmic density.

title: On Artin's conjecture
extractedQuote: In 1967, Hooley showed GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions of all number fields Q(a^{1/n}, zeta_n) implies Artin's primitive root conjecture in its quantitative form.
quoteLocator: J. Reine Angew. Math. 225 (1967), 209-220; MathOverflow Q17209 (h)
plainSummary: Proves Artin's primitive-root conjecture (e.g. 2 generates F_p* infinitely often) — requires Dedekind zeta functions of Kummer number fields, NOT covered by Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Unlocks once Dedekind ERH holds over Kummer extensions Q(a^{1/q}, zeta_q).
plainFallbackNote: Heath-Brown (1986) proved at most 2 prime bases can fail unconditionally, yet not a single specific integer (like a = 2) is unconditionally known.

title: On Euclidean rings of algebraic integers
extractedQuote: In 1973, Weinberger showed that GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions implies every ring of algebraic integers with an infinite unit group is Euclidean if it has class number 1.
quoteLocator: Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 24 (1973), 321-332; MathOverflow Q17209 (j)
plainSummary: Proves every principal-ideal number ring with infinitely many units (such as Z[sqrt(14)]) allows Euclidean division with remainder — needs Dedekind ERH, still open.
plainImpactUpgrade: Unlocks once Dedekind ERH holds across Kummer extensions.
plainFallbackNote: Harper and Murty (2004) removed ERH only when the unit group has rank >= 4, leaving real quadratic rings like Z[sqrt(14)] open.

title: Effective versions of the Chebotarev density theorem
authors: Jeffrey C. Lagarias, Andrew M. Odlyzko
extractedQuote: Sharp estimates in the Chebotarev density theorem pi_C(x) = (|C|/|G|) Li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log(|disc(L)| x^{[L:Q]})) follow from GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions.
quoteLocator: Algebraic Number Fields (Fröhlich ed., 1977), 409-464; MathOverflow Q17209 (d)
plainSummary: The master number-field theorem behind dozens of CS/algebra 'assuming GRH' papers — requires GRH for Dedekind zeta functions, NOT covered by Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Square-root effective Chebotarev error over arbitrary Galois extensions L/K holds once Dedekind ERH clears.
plainFallbackNote: Unconditional Lagarias-Odlyzko bounds hold only above huge exponential discriminant thresholds (and carry potential Stark/Siegel zero terms).

title: A bound for the least prime ideal in the Chebotarev Density Theorem
authors: Jeffrey C. Lagarias, Hugh L. Montgomery, Andrew M. Odlyzko
extractedQuote: Assuming GRH for the Dedekind zeta function zeta_L(s), every conjugacy class in Gal(L/K) is represented by an unramified prime ideal of norm <= c (log |disc(L)|)^2.
plainSummary: Bounds the smallest prime ideal in Chebotarev's theorem by O((log |disc L|)^2) — requires Dedekind zeta GRH, still open under Dirichlet-only GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Polynomial-logarithmic least-prime-ideal bound O((log |disc L|)^2) holds once Dedekind ERH clears.
plainFallbackNote: Unconditional Linnik-style bound in LMO (1979) is polynomial in |disc(L)| rather than log |disc(L)|.

title: Lower bounds for discriminants of number fields
extractedQuote: In 1975, Odlyzko showed GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions implies |disc(K)|^{1/n} >= (94.69...)^{r_1/n}(28.76...)^{2r_2/n} + o(1) (sharpened by Serre to 8 pi e^gamma = 44.763... and 8 pi e^{gamma + pi/2} = 215.33...).
plainSummary: Gives sharp root-discriminant lower bounds for number fields — relies on GRH for Dedekind zeta functions, still open.
plainImpactUpgrade: Sharp Odlyzko-Serre root-discriminant bounds hold once Dedekind ERH clears.
plainFallbackNote: Weaker unconditional Odlyzko-Poitou discriminant bounds (~22.3 and ~60.8) hold without ERH.

title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz Is in the Polynomial Hierarchy
extractedQuote: Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis [specifically Lagarias-Odlyzko effective Chebotarev for Dedekind zeta functions], Feasibility of integer polynomial systems over C lies in AM <= Pi_2^P.
plainSummary: Places polynomial system solvability over C low in the Polynomial Hierarchy (AM) — invokes Lagarias-Odlyzko effective Chebotarev over number fields, NOT Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz enters AM unconditionally once Dedekind ERH clears.
plainFallbackNote: Unconditionally Hilbert's Nullstellensatz is only known to lie in PSPACE (Canny 1988).

title: Ramanujan's ternary quadratic form
extractedQuote: In 1997, Ono and Soundararajan showed GRH for Dirichlet L-functions of quadratic characters AND for quadratic twists of the L-function of an elliptic curve over Q implies the 18 known exceptions to x^2 + y^2 + 10 z^2 are the only ones.
plainSummary: Settles all odd integers represented by x^2 + y^2 + 10z^2 — needs quadratic twists of an elliptic-curve L-function (GL(2)), NOT just Dirichlet L-functions.
plainImpactUpgrade: Once GRH extends to modular/elliptic-curve L-functions, the 18 known odd exceptions are proved complete.
plainFallbackNote: Duke and Schulze-Pillot proved unconditionally that only finitely many exceptions exist (ineffectively).

title: Polynomial-time quantum algorithms for Pell's equation and the principal ideal problem
extractedQuote: Pell's equation and the principal ideal problem are solved unconditionally in quantum polynomial time; computing the full class group of a real quadratic field uses Bach's O((log |Delta|)^2) generator bound under ERH.
plainSummary: Solves Pell's equation unconditionally on a quantum computer; computing the full number-field class group invokes Bach's Dedekind-ERH prime-ideal generator bound.
plainImpactUpgrade: Quantum polynomial-time class-group computation drops its Dedekind ERH generator assumption once number-field ERH clears.
plainFallbackNote: Pell's equation and the principal ideal test in Hallgren (2007) are already unconditional.

title: Constructing elliptic curve isogenies in quantum subexponential time
authors: Andrew M. Childs, David Jao, Vladimir Soukharev
extractedQuote: Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis [specifically Jao-Miller-Venkatesan Hecke character eigenvalue bounds and Bach's ERH class-group generators], our quantum algorithm constructs ahorizontal isogeny in L_q[1/2, sqrt(3)/2] time.
quoteLocator: J. Math. Cryptol. 8 (2014) / arXiv:1012.4019, Section 2 & Theorem 1.1
plainSummary: One of the most-cited post-quantum isogeny papers (327+ citations): assumes 'GRH', specifically Hecke-character expander bounds and Dedekind ERH class-group generators — still open.
plainImpactUpgrade: Rigorous L_q[1/2] quantum horizontal-isogeny runtime becomes unconditional once Hecke and Dedekind GRH hold.
plainFallbackNote: Without Hecke/Dedekind GRH, rigorous subexponential runtime for general ordinary curve orders remains conditional.

title: Efficient quantum algorithms for computing class groups and solving the principal ideal problem in arbitrary degree number fields
extractedQuote: Under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis [for Dedekind zeta functions via Bach's ideal-class generator bound], there is a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for S-unit groups, class groups, and PIP in arbitrary number fields.
quoteLocator: SODA 2016, pp. 893-902, Section 2 (citing Bach 1990 ERH bound)
plainSummary: Famous SODA 2016 quantum attack on ideal-lattice schemes — invokes Bach's Dedekind-ERH prime-ideal generator bound over high-degree number fields, NOT Dirichlet GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: Rigorous polynomial-time quantum class-group & S-unit computation in arbitrary number fields unlocks once Dedekind ERH clears.
plainFallbackNote: Without Dedekind ERH, small prime ideals are not guaranteed to generate Cl(O_K) in polynomial norm.

title: A Rigorous Time Bound for Factoring Integers
authors: H. W. Lenstra Jr., Carl Pomerance
extractedQuote: We prove unconditionally [eliminating the previous Generalized Riemann Hypothesis assumption via multipliers] that integers n can be factored in expected time L_n[1/2, 1 + o(1)].
plainSummary: Already unconditional! Eliminated the earlier GRH assumption from rigorous L_n[1/2, 1] integer factoring using discriminant multipliers.
plainImpactUpgrade: Already proved unconditionally in 1992; neither breaks RSA nor waits on GRH.
plainFallbackNote: Already completely unconditional since Lenstra-Pomerance (1992).

title: Linear equations in primes
extractedQuote: Full-text search hits 'assuming GRH' in historical remarks comparing Hardy-Littlewood / Balog, while Green and Tao's main linear-equations-in-primes theorem (modulo MN/GI, later proved unconditionally) does NOT assume RH or GRH.
quoteLocator: Ann. of Math. 171 (2010), Section 1 historical remarks
plainSummary: 500+ citations: surfaces in full-text 'assuming GRH' search only from a passing historical remark — Green and Tao's own prime-constellation program is unconditional.
plainImpactUpgrade: Unchanged: mentions GRH only in historical comparison; main theorem never depended on RH or GRH.
plainFallbackNote: Completed unconditionally with Green-Tao-Ziegler (2012).
